title: Prevent double-billing from fuzzy deduplication of near-duplicate stream fragments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The metering pipeline currently treats server-side fuzzy-deduplication (heuristic merging of near-duplicate response fragments) as a transparent optimization. In several customer incidents we observed duplicated billed tokens when fragments were (a) replayed by proxy, (b) partially merged by the fuzzy-merge stage, or (c) returned after a speculative rerun. We need a deterministic attribution strategy so billing is idempotent when the runtime performs approximate fragment deduplication, while keeping the optimization for latency/cost.

Goal: Design and implement a metering-safe fuzzy-dedup protocol that guarantees: (1) No double-billing for fragments that are deduplicated or merged; (2) Reasonable performance overhead (<2% p90 tail increase for streaming); (3) Observable correctness signals for production monitoring and quick rollback; (4) Back-compatibility with existing ledger anchoring used by downstream billing jobs.
updates: 2026-03-02 - Spike: ran dataset of 200k real customer streams with the fuzzy-merge staging binary (branch: eng/fuzzy-dedupe-spike). Observed 0.7% duplicate-billing rate concentrated in multi-proxy customers.

2026-03-04 - Design decision: use a hybrid approach combining stable fragment IDs (SHA256 of normalized token spans) and a probabilistic fuzzy-hash (MinHash of token shingles) to detect near-duplicates while recording canonicalization mappings to the ledger.

2026-03-06 - Tradeoff: exact-hash only approach eliminates false merges but blocks optimization for noisy transforms (whitespace, punctuation). Fuzzy-hash reduces missed merges but risks false positives; chosen mitigation is conservative similarity threshold + manual review sampling.

2026-03-08 - Implementation: added fragment_id and canonical_id to the streaming envelope header. The public ingress writes provisional ledger rows labeled 'provisional_fragment' and finalization occurs when canonical_id is known. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8123.

2026-03-10 - QA: property tests added to the metering-sim harness (scripts/metering_sim/fuzzy_cases.py) to validate idempotency across reorder, retry, partial-resend. Found rare race where two workers concurrently finalize different canonical_ids for same fragment; introduced single-writer ledger anchor per session to fix.

2026-03-12 - Prep: rollout plan drafted; feature behind FF 'fuzzy_dedupe_billing_protections' with sampling enabled at 5% initially. Observability dashboards created: Billing -> Fuzzy Dedupe Health (dashboard id: DSH-9876).
comments: Marco Chen (2026-03-03): Reviewed spike results; want to see false-positive and false-negative breakdown by model family (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder). Added metric request.
Priya Rao (Product, 2026-03-05): Customer SLA risk is high for enterprise tenants on Dedicated; prefer conservative rollout with tenant opt-out and clear communication.
Ben Liu (Security, 2026-03-07): Approach looks fine; ensure canonical_id generation only uses non-sensitive normalized tokens and salt per-tenant to avoid fingerprinting across tenants.
QA (2026-03-09): Added stress test case for concurrent finalization. Steps to repro included. Assigned follow-up to Marco.
Data Eng (2026-03-11): Will add billing joiner to map provisional_fragment rows to canonical ledger in downstream ETL. Depends on this ticket for schema changes.
Marco Chen (2026-03-12): Finished single-writer ledger anchor change; pushing integration tests now.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): FF false, sampling 5% for internal tenants only. Collect metrics and diff against baseline billing outputs.
Phase 1 (early customers): FF true for opt-in enterprise tenants and all internal workloads. Sampling 25%. Data Eng runs daily reconcilers to compare provisional->final mapping.
Phase 2 (gradual): enable for 50% of traffic, monitoring thresholds: billed_discrepancy_ratio < 0.05% and finalization_conflicts < 1/day for 7 consecutive days.
Phase 3 (global): roll out to all hosted traffic and enable backfill of canonical mappings in ledger ETL.
tests: Property tests: invariants that total billed tokens for a session after dedupe == billed tokens if dedupe disabled OR canonical mapping agrees (implemented)
Synthetic generator: replay scripts to simulate proxy replay, reordered frames, partial resend, and speculative reruns
E2E: local cluster test running billing ETL against simulated streaming ledger for 48h
Performance: microbench of hash computation and fuzzy-hash cost added to streaming p90 measurements
